method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. Every cited locator address was checked to begin an instruction of its decoded function, and the operands, name literals, vftable cells, constants and call targets named in the claims were compared with those listings by a second pass. Callers were enumerated by scanning the .text section for rel32 call and jmp instructions and the whole image for dword references, so virtual and indirect callers are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. The results of the constant switches were obtained by evaluating the functions with an interpreter that executes only compare, add, subtract, negate, subtract with borrow, and, move, zero extend and jump instructions, and the facts record counts and shapes, not the tables. The MEASURED facts are call-site counts that agree with xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json. Script argument counts, result counts and descriptor constants come from a local Lua 5.1 bytecode scan of the installed client scripts, decoded with tools/decode_lpb.py, that no tracked artifact carries, and are INFERRED. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: Static Lua call contracts of the 22 natives (23 registrations) that the unimplemented ledger lists on PlayerBase, CharaBase, DirectorBase, NpcBase, WorldMaster and GroupBase and that no other record contracts. They are the three trophy natives, seven achievement natives, _turn, _chat, _haveEnmityCharacters, _getGroupCurrent, _getExtendedTemporaryGroupCurrent, _getGroupByDisplayName on CharaBase and on DirectorBase, _getGrandOnExtraStat, _getTradingItem, _createExtendedTemporaryVirtualItem, _updateMemberAndInformation, _setMapObjScale and _cancelTransformIntoChocobo. Each row gives the registration site, the receiver type check, the declared argument and return lists, the branches, the reads, the effects on client state, the failure behavior and the yield behavior. Client-side contracts do not establish achievement, group, item, chat or scene content or server behavior.
